notes.summary: Conditional analytic unit-star construction with arbitrary residual genus: exact residual orders, global analytic lifts, finite exceptional directions, all-direction slopes and whole annular collars are proved for the supplied smooth semistable affinoid. No recognition or model-existence conclusion.
notes.detailedSummary: At an interior vertex of the supplied simply semistable model over algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued C, rational graph slopes with positive outgoing sum are realized by a scaled logarithm of an actual analytic unit. Riemann–Roch after clearing denominators gives exact prescribed orders and fresh additional zeros for arbitrary residual genus. Approximation in H(v) lifts the residual function to a quotient of global analytic functions. Their finite zero sets yield an explicit ordinary open star, including zero-order lift exceptions. Correct one-node applications of Thuillier 2.2.25 and full-fibre comparisons from 2.2.24 establish exact collar formulas. This is an unverified author proof using stated standard foundations.
notes.text:
The new analytic construction concerns an actual connected rig-smooth strict affinoid Z over algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued C, in any characteristic, with its supplied simply semistable model. Let v be an interior model vertex and R_v its smooth proper residual curve of genus g. For finitely many graph directions p_i prescribe rational slopes q_i with positive sum D_0. The construction gives an actual unit-log potential with those slopes, additional negative slopes in fresh residue directions, and zero slopes elsewhere.

The residual divisor construction retains arbitrary genus. Choose N clearing denominators with ND_0≥max(1,2g), and put E=ΣNq_i[p_i]. Riemann–Roch gives l(E)−l(E−p)=1 at every closed point p, since both K−E and K−E+p have negative degree. Thus evaluation of H⁰(O(E)) at each forbidden point is surjective. Over the infinite algebraically closed residue field, a finite union of proper evaluation kernels does not cover this vector space: the product of their nonzero linear equations is a nonzero polynomial. Choose a section outside all those kernels. As a rational function fbar, it satisfies div(fbar)=A−E, where A is effective and avoids every forbidden point. Consequently ord_{p_i}(fbar)=−Nq_i exactly, and all additional orders are positive. The actual smooth proper residual component is projective: Hartshorne I.6.9 embeds a nonsingular curve as an open subcurve of its nonsingular projective completion; properness makes that image closed and hence the whole connected completion. No degree-zero principality or genus-zero hypothesis is used.

Write Z=M(A_Z). Smooth connectedness makes A_Z an integral regular one-dimensional Noetherian affinoid algebra. A nonzero analytic function has finitely many zeros: its quotient algebra is zero-dimensional Noetherian, hence Artinian, and maximal residue fields are C by the strict affinoid Nullstellensatz. The reduced supplied model identifies the residue field of H(v) with k(R_v). Lift fbar to a norm-one element z in H(v), then approximate it by a/b, with a,b global analytic functions, so that |a(v)/b(v)−z|<1. The quotient has norm one and exactly the desired residue. Its analytic unit locus contains the ordinary open complement of the finite union P of the zero sets of a and b.

Construct the common ordinary neighborhood explicitly. Choose an open metric star S about v, missing every other vertex and the actual boundary. Shorten its graph arms before the finite set τ(P) away from v. In each exceptional non-graph residue disc |T_p|<1, choose a strict radius r_p<1 larger than the norms of all divisor points there. Delete the compact inner discs {|T_p|≤r_p} from τ⁻¹(S). The resulting W is ordinary open, contains v, lies in the actual analytic interior, and avoids P. It contains whole annular graph collars, whole outer collars in the exceptional discs, and the entire disc in every other residual direction.

The full disc and node coordinates are checked in the given étale formal charts. In a localized étale Jacobian presentation, constant lifts of the selected residual coordinates have equation error q<1 on each strict closed subdisc or subannulus. The Jacobian inverse has norm at most one. Banach Newton errors are bounded by q^(2^j), giving analytic inverses on the entire strict subdomains. Linear-term estimates prove uniqueness among solutions with the selected residue, also after evaluation in every completed residue field. The inverses agree on overlaps, whose ordinary interiors exhaust the tubes. This handles nonrigid points and arbitrary characteristic without taking an adic completion at the non-finitely-generated residue maximal ideal of C°.

For the slope calculation, make actual type-2 cuts before P in every selected direction using the explicit admissible blowups (T_p,c_p), or the corresponding node subdivision. These preserve R_v and create adjacent nodes at its original residual points. Each selected full node tube avoids P. In that common refined model, remove other nodes and reductions of P, retaining a connected formal open with exactly one singular point. The quotient is a unit on its entire generic fibre. Thuillier tel-00010990v1, Lemma 2.2.25, therefore applies with its stated hypotheses and gives outgoing slope −ord_p(fbar). This formal open is used only for the published slope computation; W is the separately constructed ordinary neighborhood.

Exhaust every selected open collar by strict closed subannuli. Thuillier Proposition 2.2.24(ii),(iii) gives equality on every full retraction fibre and zero trace Laplacian. Its trace is therefore affine, with intercept zero by continuity at v and the computed slope. Hence G(v)+N⁻¹log|a/b| has precisely the graph slopes q_i and fresh slopes −m_p/N, where A=Σm_p[p]. These are equalities on entire annuli, not only their skeletal paths.

Outside the finite exceptional set, both a and b are nonzero on the entire residue disc. On each nested strict closed Gauss disc, f and f⁻¹ attain their maxima at the unique Shilov point. The two inequalities force |f| constant there; nesting and continuity to v give |f|=1 on the whole open disc. Additional lift directions of residual order zero have an exact constant outer collar, even if zeros of a or b lie deeper. They can therefore be continued by that constant without asserting an unavailable full-disc unit.

The boundary identity is checked separately. Van der Put (1980), Theorem 1.1, applies to this normal connected strict affinoid over algebraically closed C and embeds the same affinoid in a nonsingular complete algebraic curve. Berkovich (1993), Theorem 1.6.1 and Lemma 1.6.2(i), identifies the same analytic domain. Thuillier 2.1.10/2.1.12 then identify its actual ordinary interior and Shilov boundary. This published foundation supplies no new model, tree or factorization.

Foundations and applications are stated in P06.2-partial.tex: BGR Sections 6.1.2/7.3 for affinoid algebra facts, EGA IV Section 17.6 for the étale Jacobian criterion, Hartshorne IV.1.3/1.4 for Riemann–Roch, and the supplied-model geometry and unit slope proofs in Thuillier. Complete selected primary bodies, source hashes and inclusive literal LF coordinates are directly included in P06.2-argument.md and recorded in evidence/source-selections.json. The installed Thuillier text hash is e82226b3dde6a8088c35e1481bfd43f64bb69ee309b5cfda92c8c927a7885570. Its full 2.3.22 proof was inspected, but its germ exact sequence is not used as a grant of the new lifting application.

This conditional construction does not recognize arbitrary continuous zero-current functions, construct models or trees for arbitrary germs, or solve original P06.2. Rerun bash reproduce.sh in the assigned workspace. Source integrity and execution success do not certify mathematical correctness.

notes.text:
Exact conditional theorem. Let C be algebraically closed, complete and nontrivially valued in any characteristic. Let Z be the supplied actual connected rig-smooth strict affinoid curve, with its supplied simply semistable model, finite metric TREE Γ, actual Shilov boundary B and retraction τ. Let F be finite, real, continuous, edgewise affine and harmonic on Γ\B. For each σ∈{1,−1}, the author proof constructs u_n^σ continuous on Z, ordinary CLD-smooth psh on Ω=Int(Z), decreasing uniformly on Z to σF∘τ. For every supplied compact strict affinoid Y⊂Ω, the restricted sequences live on that SAME Y, and every approximant is ordinarily smooth on the actual ordinary open neighborhood Ω. Boundary values are continuous, but need not equal the target boundary values at finite stages. Ordinary smooth harmonic approximants are not asserted.

Proof. Use the original formal-model vertices and exclude only the actual B. Harmonic redundant degree-two subdivisions, including type-3 points, can be removed; no type-3 point is promoted to a model vertex. For a singleton Γ the target is constant. Otherwise root the tree at b∈B, put μ=1 on interior vertices I, μ(b)=−|I| and μ=0 elsewhere on B. Prescribe each child-subtree μ sum as its child-to-parent slope and integrate to obtain ψ. Subtracting child-subtree sums shows Δψ=μ, hence Δψ=1 on I. Perturb H=σF by a small δψ, rationally round its oriented slopes, and integrate along unique tree paths. If rounding error is η, uniform error is at most total edge length times η, and outgoing-sum error is at most valency times η. Thus one obtains G arbitrarily close to H, with rational slopes and strictly positive outgoing sums at interior vertices. This elementary calculation is reproved as support, not counted as a new analytic result.

At each interior vertex apply n1. The potential H_v=G(v)+N_v⁻¹log|f_v| on one actual ordinary unit star has exactly the graph slopes and additional negative slopes only in finitely many fresh full residue discs. On every whole graph collar it equals G∘τ exactly. Zero-order lift exceptions have exact constant outer collars and are continued by G(v); every remaining full residue disc has that constant. Shorten the finitely many graph stars so they are disjoint and miss B. Real intercepts are allowed smooth functions of actual unit moments; the real target slopes are preserved through the approximation errors.

Cap each fresh direction. In its full residue disc |T|<1, the available collar potential is c−at, with a>0 and t=−log|T|. For an even smooth probability density ρ supported in (−1,1), put χ_η(x)=∫|x−ηs|ρ(s)ds and M_η(x,y)=(x+y+χ_η(x−y))/2. This is smooth convex, nondecreasing in both variables, equals max when |x−y|≥η, and differs from max by at most η/2. Choose parameters with 0<η<ar/2, r+η/a smaller than the available collar length ℓ, and ar+η/2 smaller than the required error. On the entire ordinary open annulus e^(−ℓ)<|T|<1 use q(t)=M_η(c−at,c−ar). It equals c−at for 0<t<r−η/a and the NEW constant c−ar for t>r+η/a. Continue by c−ar on the ordinary inner open disc |T|<e^(−s), where r+η/a<s<ℓ. The annulus and inner disc cover the full residue disc and agree on the entire open plateau overlap s<t<ℓ. Shorten the central star cut to t_0<r−η/a; its overlap with the cap is then the full annulus 0<t<t_0 with exact affine equality. The cap annulus excludes v, which remains covered by the central actual unit germ. No old plateau restoration or psh partition gluing occurs.

On each entire original open-edge annulus use the affine graph formula G∘τ. It agrees with endpoint star formulas on full ordinary annular overlaps. Residue discs attached inside an edge are already included in that full annulus. Vertex residue discs are constant, zero-order-exception constant, or capped as above. These sets give an actual ordinary open cover of Ω, including type-3 and type-4 points. At B the function is G∘τ near the vertex and is continuous; no artificial boundary is introduced. Exact agreement defines one g continuous on Z and ordinarily smooth on Ω. Outside fresh discs g=G∘τ; each fresh-disc error relative to G(v) is below its tolerance. Combining graph and cap errors makes ||g−H∘τ|| on Z arbitrarily small.

Positivity holds for EVERY ordinary test. Central actual unit-log potentials, affine edge moment coordinates and constants have zero smooth Hessian. In a cap chart, d'd''g=q''(t)d't∧d''t with q''≥0. Exact ordinary open agreement eliminates interface distributions. In an arbitrary common moment chart for a nonnegative compact ordinary scalar test φ and the cap, each calibrated one-dimensional cell has its actual positive multiplicity m_α, primitive tangent coordinate ξ, and t=A_αξ+c_α. Its contribution is m_αφq''(t)A_α²dξ≥0. Collapsed directions contribute zero; they are not omitted. The smooth reduced curve has generic length one, and the algebraically closed residue field makes the actual original semistable edge weights one. Higher moment degrees, including inseparable degrees, remain in the canonical calibration. CLD positive integration and Green duality on boundaryless Ω give ∫g d'd''φ=∫φ d'd''g≥0 for every compact nonnegative ordinary scalar test. This uses actual ordinary unit charts, not weak smoothness or a pullback of a continuous current to curves.

For each sign choose raw g_n^σ with error b_n=4^(−n) on the entire same Z. Set c_n=Σ_{j≥n}(b_j+b_{j+1})=(5/3)b_n and u_n^σ=g_n^σ+c_n. Since c_n−c_{n+1}=b_n+b_{n+1}, the error bounds imply u_n^σ≥u_{n+1}^σ and 0≤u_n^σ−σh≤(8/3)b_n. Constants preserve ordinary smoothness and psh. Neither the domain nor Y shrinks, and both signs use the same Z and Ω.

The essential CLD foundations have their exact hypotheses checked: ordinary charts in 1204.6277v2 Proposition 15.1.1(b)/Corollary 15.1.2, canonical positive integration in 7.3.1–7.3.4, Green in Proposition 5.11.1 with compact support intersection, and analytic-interior harmony in Theorem 15.6.1. Complete selected primary bodies, exact LF coordinates and body hashes appear directly in P06.2-argument.md, together with every new supporting proof. GJR2111.05741v3 supplies the actual semistable weight convention, not a unit-germ theorem grant.

Limitations: the harmonic factorization, actual affinoid, model and tree are INPUTS. This result does not derive them from arbitrary continuous zero-current functions, establish all-point model/tree realization, treat singular or nonreduced curves, prove scalar-current ascent, solve the all-curve gate or solve unchanged original P06.2.
